title: A/B routing header mismatch caused split-traffic regression and blocked rollback
creator: Maya Patel
description: Post-incident follow-up for a model rollout that caused an unintended A/B split and prevented an automated rollback. A header encoding mismatch in the edge proxy caused the router to misclassify traffic, and a race between rollout controller and version pinning logic left the cluster in a mixed state. This ticket captures timeline, root cause, mitigation, and a prioritized action list with owners.
timeline: 2026-03-09 08:12 UTC - Rollout initiated: Variant B deployed to canary pool (rv=2026-03-09-canary).
2026-03-09 08:14 UTC - Edge proxy upgrade 1.3.5 rolled out to ingress nodes (included a header encoding change).
2026-03-09 08:17 UTC - Monitoring alert: error rate on key customer route rose from 0.2% -> 4%.
2026-03-09 08:19 UTC - Pager duty: oncall investigating; initial hypothesis was model regression in Variant B.
2026-03-09 08:26 UTC - Temporary canary swap attempted (rollback); controller rejected swap due to active version_pins for several tenants.
2026-03-09 08:34 UTC - Manual investigation found inconsistent X-Model-Variant header values (some encoded as base64 by proxy).
2026-03-09 08:45 UTC - Emergency mitigation: scale up stable variant instances and enable transparent fallback routing. Customer impact reduced but not fully resolved.

2026-03-09 09:10 UTC - Root cause identified: routing regex and header decoder mismatch introduced by proxy upgrade; rollout controller logic did not clear soft pins automatically leading to rollback failure.
2026-03-09 10:05 UTC - Hotfix deployed: proxy reverted header encoding change and rollout controller patched to attempt an automated unpin step on explicit failed rollback (canary -> stable).
root_cause: Two converging issues: (1) Edge proxy 1.3.5 introduced an unexpected change to how X-Model-Variant header values were encoded (base64 in some paths), causing the router's A/B matching regex to misclassify requests and split traffic unevenly. (2) Rollout controller treats user version_pins as authoritative and will not perform a rollback that would violate active pins; when the automated rollback failed, controller entered a blocked state instead of performing a safe fallback, because there was no unpin-on-failure policy and no operator-visible alert tied to blocked rollouts.
mitigation: Immediate: Revert proxy header encoding change on ingress nodes (rolled back to 1.3.4) to restore deterministic header values (COMPLETE).
Immediate: Scale up stable variant pool by 2x and enable explicit fallback route for affected customer prefixes (COMPLETE).

Short-term: Deploy controller patch that will attempt an automated 3-step unpin sequence (notify owner -> dry-run unpin -> unpin) when a rollback is manually triggered and the pin appears stale (IN REVIEW).
Short-term: Add an alert that surfaces blocked rollouts due to active version_pins and notify PM/owner channel (IN PROGRESS).
Long-term: Tighten routing header contract and add end-to-end tests between proxy, router, and controller in CI to catch mismatched encodings (TODO).
action_items: ENG-22451: Add canonical header parser and validation in router library; include unit tests for base64/unencoded variants — owner: Liam Chen — due: 2026-03-18
ENG-22452: Implement automated unpin flow in rollout controller with audit log and operator approval step — owner: Priya Rao — due: 2026-03-21
ENG-22453: Add end-to-end CI job that spins up proxy+router+controller and runs smoke test for a sample canary rollback path — owner: Diego Martinez — due: 2026-04-01
ENG-22454: Update runbook: blocked rollouts runbook with one-click unpin checklist and Slack alert links — owner: Oncall Rotation — due: 2026-03-16
ENG-22455: Create a dashboard panel showing 'blocked rollouts due to pins' and wire it to incident channel — owner: SRE Team — due: 2026-03-17
notes: PM feedback (2026-03-11): Prioritize customer-visible mitigations and a postmortem summary for affected customers. - Katerina Volkova
